parallel.requirements: The parent recognized the ESM .mjs, no external dependency, manual argv, canonicaljson, byte repr, pretty-print, BigInt, float-repr, and no JSON stringify/parse requirements before delegation.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent first probed reference behavior, then split the work into seven file-owned child tasks: pyfloat, pyint, pyescape, pybytes, canonicaljson, argparse, and test10 entry point.
parallel.implementation: Children wrote the assigned modules independently. After the swarm returned, the parent ran integration checks, found a float representation mismatch caused by V8 rounding semantics, and directly edited pyfloat.mjs; it also cleaned an argparse comment.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent joined all child outputs through the AgentSwarm aggregate, ran whole-program comparison scripts from the shared /output tree, and delivered the expected test10.mjs plus lib modules.
parallel.verification: Verification included reference probes, node --check per child, a 56-case end-to-end comparison, fuzz testing that first found two mismatches, a pyfloat fix, a rerun with PASS=56 FAIL=0 and fuzz failures 0, and an additional targeted fuzz with zero failures.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The final official evaluator still marked the artifact as failing 31 of 139 cases. The mounted evidence does not reveal those hidden cases; the visible process does not show an unjoined child result or unrepaired child-created mismatch at closure.

serial.requirements: The serial agent recognized the same ESM .mjs, zero dependency, manual argv, canonicaljson, byte repr, pretty printing, BigInt, Python float representation, and error-code requirements.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One agent owned all probing, implementation, integration, verification, and delivery, writing pyformat, jsonescape, encoder, argparse, and test10 sequentially.
serial.implementation: The serial agent implemented primitives, JSON escaping, canonical and pretty encoding, argparse emulation, and the entry point; after a comparison harness exposed a bare -- mismatch, it edited argparse.mjs.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial work was integrated as it was written in a single workspace and delivered as test10.mjs plus four library modules.
serial.verification: Verification included reference probes, a targeted comparison harness that initially reported 51 pass and 4 fail, a parser fix, a rerun with PASS=55 FAIL=0, 300 random fuzz cases with zero failures, and import/dependency checks.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The final official evaluator still marked the artifact as failing 31 of 139 cases. The hidden failing cases are not present in the mounted evidence, so the remaining defect is not attributable to a documented coordination boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel parent identified the main behavior requirements from the prompt and its probes, including bytes repr, float repr, arbitrary precision integers, argparse errors, and chunk count.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial agent identified the same task requirements through the prompt and local probes before writing modules.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-recognition difference is evidenced; both local strategies targeted the same visible obligations and both officially failed hidden cases.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run assigned seven distinct owners for seven files through AgentSwarm, with each child constrained to one exact output path.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run kept all module design, implementation, integration, and final delivery under one actor.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel attempt used file-level decomposition, while the serial control used single-agent sequential ownership; both had implementation and delivery owners.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent provided a shared contract in the swarm prompt, including value conventions, exact exports, local import restrictions, and per-file responsibilities; child returns reported the implemented exports.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial agent carried the interfaces internally while writing all modules in one flow and did not need cross-agent handoffs.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had explicit cross-file contracts for child work; serial had implicit single-agent interface continuity. No incompatible child handoff survived to closure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children created the modules and entry point, then the parent modified pyfloat.mjs after fuzzing showed a CPython float-rounding mismatch.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial agent wrote fewer combined modules and fixed argparse.mjs after its harness exposed a bare -- behavior mismatch.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both produced similar behavioral coverage by different implementation layouts; the only visible repaired bug differs, but neither final official failure is uniquely tied to parallel decomposition.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: All seven child tasks returned through the AgentSwarm aggregate before the parent proceeded to whole-program verification and edits.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: There were no delegated results to retrieve; each local write immediately remained in the serial agent's workspace for the next step.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had an explicit join point and consumed the returned work; serial had no child lifecycle. No missing join or trapped verifier result is evidenced.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Each child wrote a distinct file; after the joined result, the parent operated on the assembled /output tree and edited pyfloat.mjs and argparse.mjs in a non-concurrent integration phase.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial agent wrote all final files sequentially in the shared output directory and then edited argparse.mjs after testing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel used a shared workspace but with file-level separation and post-join parent edits; serial used a single writer. No live write collision, overwrite consequence, or provenance loss is visible.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel verification escalated from child syntax checks to parent end-to-end reference comparison and fuzzing; a float mismatch was caught, repaired, and followed by successful reruns.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial verification used reference comparison, detected a parser mismatch, repaired it, then ran a 55-case harness, 300 random fuzz cases, and import checks.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both relied on local oracle-style testing rather than the official hidden evaluator during the run, and both closed with local tests passing but official status failing.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used 1,359 agent seconds, did not time out, completed seven subagents, and left enough time for integration tests, fixes, and final targeted fuzzing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used 1,406 agent seconds, did not time out, completed without subagents, and similarly left time for repairs and fuzzing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There is no evidence that parallel fan-out or waiting consumed the closure budget; both runs completed and failed the official evaluator at the same rate.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluation is a both_fail outcome: both artifacts are marked solution_passed false with 108/139 samples passing. The process evidence shows different work organization but not a concrete parallel-only task-solving loss: the parallel parent joined child outputs, found and fixed a child-created float mismatch through end-to-end fuzzing, and closed with local checks passing, while the serial agent independently closed with local checks passing. The mounted evidence does not expose the official hidden failing cases, so the shared failure is best treated as an ordinary remaining implementation/coverage gap rather than a parallel coordination pattern.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel used separate files for pyint, pyfloat, pyescape, pybytes, canonicaljson, argparse, and the entry point, while serial combined formatting primitives into pyformat and used a smaller module set.
Parallel repaired a float representation bug after fuzzing; serial repaired an argparse bare -- behavior mismatch after its comparison harness.
evaluator_effects: The official evaluator reports the common 108/139 result but the mounted pair does not include the hidden failing case details, so the exact residual semantic mismatch cannot be resolved from allowed inputs.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; supported process contrast only
